final_candidates.decision_summary: Highest pathogenicity LOF signal (z=0.996) with well-covered MSA showing low tolerance; strongest convergent LOF candidate.
Very high pathogenicity (z=0.987) reinforced by low MSA tolerance and ESM-1v disfavoring; strong LOF at a conserved catalytic-region residue.
Strong pathogenicity (z=0.979) and lowest MSA tolerance at a conserved Gly; bulky Arg into buried Gly is strongly disruptive to fold and function.

stop_reason.detail: Evidence has converged and remaining applicable tools cannot meaningfully alter the Top-3.

history.rationale: Lys119 is the conserved Schiff-base lysine that covalently binds the PLP cofactor; substitution abolishes cofactor anchoring and catalysis.
K119 is the PLP-binding lysine (Schiff base); pathogenicity 0.987 confirms catalytic essentiality, keeping it top-tier.
Highest pathogenicity LOF signal (z=0.987) reinforced by very low MSA tolerance (A freq 0.056) and ESM-1v disfavoring the mutation; strong LOF convergence.
Thr257 lies in the highly conserved catalytic core region; disrupting it likely impairs substrate/cofactor coordination and reduces activity.
Pathogenicity 0.913 consistent but T-to-A is conservative, limiting confidence in full LOF.
Highest evolutionary tolerance in the pool (A freq 0.238, well-covered) undercuts LOF likelihood despite decent pathogenicity; weakest candidate now.

rejection.reason: Highest evolutionary tolerance in the pool (A freq 0.238, well-covered) undercuts LOF likelihood despite decent pathogenicity; weakest candidate now.

history.rationale: Gly259 sits in a conserved glycine-rich active-site loop; a bulky charged residue would sterically disrupt the fold and catalytic geometry.
Pathogenicity 0.975 with a bulky charged substitution at a conserved glycine; strong LOF signal.
High pathogenicity (z=0.975) and low MSA tolerance with strong coverage; consistent LOF candidate.
Asp309 in the conserved PLP-binding region likely coordinates catalytic contacts; charge reversal should abolish function.
Pathogenicity 0.896 remains supportive but lowest among charge-reversal candidates.
Lower pathogenicity (z=0.896) and moderate MSA tolerance; kept as backup below the leaders.
Gly307 in the GVDP motif is conserved for backbone flexibility near the active site; large substitution disrupts local structure.
High pathogenicity (0.979) plus a disruptive Gly-to-Arg substitution favors strong LOF; upgraded.
Strong pathogenicity (z=0.979) and lowest MSA tolerance (A/R freq 0.029, entropy 2.09) at conserved Gly; bulky Arg into buried Gly strongly disruptive.
Asn149 in the conserved TSGNTG catalytic motif may contribute to PLP/substrate positioning; mutation likely reduces activity.
Highest LOF-proxy pathogenicity (0.996); AlphaMissense strongly predicts damaging, consistent with active-site region.
Top pathogenicity signal (z=0.996) with well-covered MSA (app 0.98) showing low tolerance; promoted above G307R.
Arg336 is a conserved active-site arginine likely important for substrate carboxylate binding; loss should reduce activity.
Pathogenicity 0.957 supports LOF but slightly below the top glycine/catalytic candidates.
Good pathogenicity (z=0.957) but MSA evidence is nearly uninformative (coverage 12/87, app 0.14), lowering supporting confidence.
Thr191 near the PLP phosphate-binding region may stabilize cofactor; substitution could weaken binding and activity.
Pathogenicity 0.714 is clearly the weakest LOF signal; conservative T-to-A likely tolerated.

rejection.reason: Pathogenicity 0.714 is clearly the weakest LOF signal; conservative T-to-A likely tolerated.

history.rationale: His203 in a conserved region may participate in catalysis or cofactor interaction; mutation plausibly impairs enzyme function.
Pathogenicity 0.920 higher than prior estimate; modest upgrade.
Pathogenicity z=0.920 plus very low MSA tolerance (freq 0.036, app 0.95) at a conserved His; promoted above R336A.
